title: Food and Shopping
grammar_title: Grammar: Countable / uncountable · some / any · How much? How many? · I'd like…

plan.listen: VOA Lesson 21: Can You Come to the Party?
VOA Lesson 23: What Do You Want? + British Council: “Booking a table” (listening)
BBC Real Easy English: “Talking about shopping” (video)

sentences: I'd like a cup of tea, please.
أريد كوبًا من الشاي من فضلك.
How much is this? — It's fifty pounds.
بكم هذا؟ — بخمسين جنيهًا.
Can I have the bill, please?
الحساب من فضلك.
We need some eggs and some bread.
نحتاج إلى بعض البيض وبعض الخبز.
Is there any milk in the fridge?
هل يوجد حليب في الثلاجة؟
How many apples do you want?
كم تفاحة تريد؟
It's too expensive. Do you have a cheaper one?
إنه غالٍ جدًا. هل لديك واحد أرخص؟
Can I pay by card?
هل يمكنني الدفع بالبطاقة؟
I don't eat much sugar.
لا آكل الكثير من السكر.
This food is delicious!
هذا الطعام لذيذ!

grammar.intro_en:
some in positive sentences and offers (Would you like some tea?) · any in negatives and questions (I don't have any rice. Is there any milk?)
How much is it? = asking the price.
grammar.intro_ar: «بكم؟» = How much is it? · وفي المطعم الأدب أن تقول …I'd like أو …Can I have بدلًا من I want.

rows: an apple → two apples · How many apples?
water, rice, bread, milk, money (no a, no -s) · How much water?

write_speak:
Write & Speak — Write a 6-line conversation in a café or shop. Read both parts aloud, then act it out with someone.
Example: A: Good evening. Can I help you? — B: Yes, I'd like a cup of tea, please. — A: Anything else? — B: A piece of cake, please. How much is it? — A: It's ninety pounds. — B: Here you are. Thank you!
